fields.headline: STATE PICKS PARAVISION FOR ID CHECKS
fields.deck: The contract can run through 2031 with a potential value of $6.5 million.

frames.mediaQuery: Paravision facial recognition deepfake detection identity verification

stories.caption:
A five-year State Department contract with facial recognition developer Paravision could be worth as much as $6.5 million. Federal procurement records list the work as "digital detection/identity assurance," and the department awarded it September 23 with an initial obligation of $1.3 million.

The contract runs through September 22, 2031, and was competed as a total small-business set-aside under simplified acquisition procedures, with one offer received. Public award records do not name the Paravision products involved. The description lines up with the company's deepfake detection and passive liveness detection tools, but the records do not confirm whether those, its facial recognition software or other products are included.

A separate $24,717 purchase order to Paravision on April 30 was labeled a "purchase card for software license." Public records do not show whether that buy was a test, a pilot or a step toward the September contract.

Source: Biometric Update, 17OCT26

fields.headline: XTEND LANDS $40.5M STRIKER DRONE BUY
fields.deck: The order follows a top-performer finish in Gauntlet II of the Drone Dominance Program.

stories.caption:
XTEND AI Robotics has received a $40.5 million order for 6,000 STRIKER drones. The company was named a top performer in the Close Quarters Battle segment of Gauntlet II in the U.S. Department of War's iterative $1 billion Drone Dominance Program. XTEND's chief executive, Aviv Shapira, said, "We competed, we proved our capabilities, and now we are ready to build."

STRIKER runs on XTEND's proprietary XOS operating system and is built for tactical missions in confined, complex and GNSS-denied environments. Gauntlet II awardees advance straight to Gauntlet III in the Close Quarters Battle segment of Phase 3, which opened September 28, 2026, but first must fill a 400-system production order. The company says Gauntlet III performance will decide whether any Phase 3 orders are placed, and that taking part does not guarantee an award.

XTEND also released preliminary third quarter 2026 revenue and a backlog update in its release. Those figures are not covered here.

Source: XTEND AI Robotics, October 13, 2026

fields.headline: ARMY TO TEST COUNTER-DRONE GEAR IN AFRICA
fields.deck: Soldiers will evaluate emerging systems in Morocco and aim to field them within 180 days.

stories.caption:
The U.S. Army Southern European Task Force, Africa (SETAF-AF) is working with the Army's Global Tactical Edge Acquisition Directorate (G-TEAD) to put new systems through trials on the continent and get them into Soldiers' hands quickly.

The first accelerated capability event is set for spring 2027 in Tan-Tan, Morocco. It targets protection for early-entry command posts and operating locations against Group 1–3 small UAS. The Army says Africa's open spectrum and uncongested airspace let Soldiers validate solutions in theater, conditions it says training ranges in the United States and Europe cannot easily match.

Under a three-phase model, teams move from submission and preparation to Soldier-led demonstrations, then to follow-on operational evaluation. SETAF-AF plans a Soldier-led demonstration in February and March 2027, then an operational assessment in spring 2027 during African Lion, the U.S. Africa Command exercise. G-TEAD will validate up to 15 solutions with PAE Fires as the transition partner.

Source: U.S. Army, October 16, 2026

fields.headline: PENTAGON OFFERS ANTHEIA $80M LOAN
fields.deck: The conditional commitment would support its U.S. drug ingredient manufacturing.

stories.caption:
The Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital has issued Antheia a conditional commitment for a direct, long-term loan of up to $80 million. Antheia, an advanced biosynthesis company, says the financing, alongside additional private capital, would support its plan to onshore production of critical pharmaceutical ingredients.

Most of the country's supply of key starting materials and active pharmaceutical ingredients comes from foreign suppliers, a dependence Antheia says leaves patients exposed to shortages during public health emergencies, natural disasters, geopolitical tensions and supply chain failures.

The commitment is conditional. Antheia must meet financial, legal, technical, investment and due diligence requirements before financial close. The company previously reported $32 million in non-dilutive federal financing and equity from strategic government-affiliated investors.

Source: PR Newswire, 18 Oct 2026
